hypothesis: Increasing required_margin never turns a failing verdict into a passing one: CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN and meets_required_margin are nonincreasing in the declared margin, non-certifying codes and inequality_certified do not depend on it, and the switch to MARGIN_LOW happens exactly at required_margin = margin.
input_data: 24 near-threshold cases (PCG64 seed 108) plus four robust cases and 8 razor-edge cases (seed 1081)
Per case: required margins {0, res/2, res, 2 res, 1e300} and, when the margin is positive, {margin/2, nextafter(margin, 0), margin, nextafter(margin, inf), 2 margin}
mathematical_model: The declared margin r enters the decision order only in the branch margin > res, as MARGIN_LOW iff margin <= r; meets_required_margin = margin > max(r, res). Both are monotone in r by construction; negative or non-finite r must be refused.
numerical_result: 280 verdicts over 36 cases: violations {'passing_regained': 0, 'meets_regained': 0, 'noncertifying_code_changed': 0, 'inequality_changed': 0}; threshold mismatches 0; invalid margins {'-1e-300': 'raises ValueError', '-1': 'raises ValueError', 'nan': 'raises ValueError', 'inf': 'raises ValueError'}. No counterexample to monotonicity was found (a finite search, not a proof).
